A player starts with 3 ships; a bonus ship is awarded at 10,000 points and every 50,000 points. The game ends when all ships have been destroyed. Good luck!

201264.overview: Six-Gun Shootout is a turn-based strategy game of man-to-man combat, using the setting of the American West in the 19th century. It offers ten scenarios which can be played against the computer or a human opponent. The scenarios are loosely based on historical situations, like the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral, or entirely fictional. Some are based on movies, for example the 1959 released "Rio Bravo". The characters engaging each other are split into two factions called "Good Guys" and Bad Guys", and are rated in different categories, such as their accuracy with weapons. It's possible to play a customized character. The game's tactical combat engine has features such as line-of sight, postures, terrain and wound effects, and includes 18 weapons with different attributes. A scenario is won by the player with the most victory points, which are accumulated by killing or incapacitating opposing individuals. It's possible for a side to be completely wiped out, yet be the winner through this system.

201280.overview:
Space Harrier is a homebrew conversion of the 16bit game to Atari 8-bit series. It is widely recognized for its capture of the gameplay of the original and stretching the Atari hardware to its limits with fast action 3D perspective, digitized sound, and colorful presentation. 

Like the arcade game, it is a fast-paced rail shooter game played in a third-person perspective behind the protagonist, set in a surreal world composed of brightly colored landscapes adorned with checkerboard-style grounds and stationary objects such as trees or stone pillars.

201307.overview:
The Atari version is a homebrew conversion from C64 source; it has been enhanced to run in high color if you VBXE addon, but will work equally well on a regular A8 machine.

Spectipede is a Centipede clone. The object of the game is to play for as long as possible to achieve a high score. The Spectipede starts out at the top of the screen and works its way down, changing direction whenever it encounters an obstacle such as a tree, mushroom or the edge of the screen. The player is at the bottom of the screen and must shoot the Spectipede before it reaches the bottom of the screen and they are devoured. Whenever the Spectipede is shot it will break into two pieces which will move independently. In addition to the Spectipede itself, fleas will jump from the beast and descend towards the player. 

These require two shots to kill them and they speed up when first hit. As the fleas descend they drop mushrooms onto the screen. Also roaming across the screen are scorpions. These poison the mushrooms and any Spectipede hitting a poisoned mushroom will immediately drop to the bottom of the screen towards the player. The player must also watch out for a spider which makes random appearances and tries to attack the player. Points are scored for each Spectipede segment, flea, scorpion and spider killed with a bonus awarded when an entire screen is cleared. The player starts with three lives and an extra life is awarded for every 20,000 points scored.

201323.overview:
There are two "Star Maze" games for the A8, this is the first one released and more popular (the other is an educational game from Roklan). 

The object of Star Maze is to collect the nine jewels in a large, randomly generated, maze-like structure.

The player flies through the maze in a spaceship that looks and controls like the ship from Atari's Asteroids arcade game: one button applies thrust, the other button shoots in the direction the ship is pointing. The joystick orients the ship. A hyperspace key drops the ship in a random location in the maze, and a finite number of antimatter bombs (R key) destroy all visible enemies. Unlike Asteroids, the ship has limited fuel, and the hyperspace option uses a significant amount of it. A jewel can only be collected it the ship's speed is below a certain threshold, then the jewel can be flown to the mothership in exchange for additional fuel.

Completing a maze gives a bonus based on how much time it took. There are 16 levels.

205333.overview:
Survival Adventure is a text adventure for multiple systems.

You have been dropped off in the jungle wilderness by a helicopter, armed only with a supply of food. The player must attempt to survive a set number of days, while trying to find the four diamonds which are lost in the jungle. During this search, the player must contend with environmental hazards including rainstorms, floods, thirst, and heat exhaustion. The player must sleep during the nights, or they will be too weak to continue, and must also discover appropriate shelter. Each turn typically takes one hour, and time is displayed at the top of the screen

The game has a difficulty level from 1 - 9, which determines how frequent and dangerous the environmental dangers are. The player has a total of 12 - 18 days to find all the treasures, before the helicopter returns to pick up the player again. All commands are via VERB NOUN commands, and the player has a small available inventory. There is a save and restore feature available.

210864.overview:
S.A.G.A. #6: Strange Odyssey is an update of the text-only version. It had many additional features including: Hi-Res graphics, Text-to-Speech hardware support, upper- and lowercase support for display (but not for input).

Gameplay is very similar to the original. You still used the same one or two word commands to move about and manipulate objects. The RETURN key toggled back and forth between graphics and text.

 The game begins with the player stranded on a tiny asteroid in a damaged spaceship. The player must use an alien teleportation device to travel to distant worlds, collect treasure, and find the materials to repair the spacecraft.

212142.overview: Big Bird's Funhouse is a "concentration" style game where the player memorizes various Sesame Street characters as they are revealed in order to select them later. The original game came with a pack-in keyboard cover that would identify keys that equated to the various characters (to press when they appear).

214274.overview:
Stickybear Numbers is an education number game for young children.

Based upon the Stickybear series of games for children, the game helps young children learn their numbers. The player can select numbers from 0 - 9, and the appropriate number of items are displayed on the screen. The player can see bouncing balls, rocket ships, toy trucks, and more with colorful animated graphics.

215200.overview:
This is a standard text-parser adventure game similar to others in the genre at the time, with an action/noun two word parser. The game is closely modeled from the movie "The Black Hole" (1979), however it is not an official license. Several characters seen in the movie appear, and the general setting is the same.  The game has approximately 30 locations, so is mid-sized for adventures of the time.

The crew of an interstellar craft discovers the long-lost Deep-Space Probe One, the Cygnus, at the edge of the vortex surrounding an immense black hole. See if you can foil the plans of Dr. Hans Reinhardt. 

Part of a continuing series of adventures published by the magazine Softside (but also available directly ordered without the magazine).

418723.overview:
King Michael has promised the hand of marriage to Princess Clare to anyone who can save her from Spooky Castle. You, Gormless Gary, has taken up the challenge and entered the castle. To hinder Gary in his quest, there are bats and ghosts flying about with fire scattered around also. Touching any of these reduces Gary's energy bar. When the bar is empty, then it's game over when all lives are lost. Scattered around the castle though are crosses which give extra lives, potions which give Gary more energy and keys which open doors.

Spooky Castle is a flick screen platform game. Each screen shows a small part of the castle. The joystick or keyboard is used to control Gary. As well as the main playing area you can see your energy bar, keys and crosses collected.

418724.overview:
Spellicopter is an educational software game that enables children to develop their spelling skills in order to remain in flight. The screen display shows speed, altitude, fuel level, score and cargo. It offers three levels of difficulty, allowing the student to learn up to 400 words, in 40 categories, in beginner, intermediate and advanced modes.

The program could be played using keyboard or joystick, giving a sentence context clue for each word, allowing the student to maintain altitude and speed for correct spellings, utilizing screen graphics, animation and sound effects.

418727.overview: Screwball has 60 seconds to changes the color of all the squares on the screen by hopping between them. The player is menaced by the Black Bugs, which chase the player around the maze, and cost the player a life if caught. Screwball can dig holes in the maze to drop bugs through, and if surrounded can hyperspace to the top of the screen, although, this can cost a life. When all squares change color, the player advances to the next level.

418761.overview:
You were successful police officer Alan Chance, until you were killed during a raid on drug dealers, who managed to take a hostage in the process. People have assumed that you died as a result of your own mistakes.

Now you have returned as a ghost, with psychic powers in place of your physical ones. Starting out at your own funeral, you must follow conversations to find clues. One early task is to find items which boost your physical abilities. You have help from other deceased beings, starting with pub owner Joe Danby.

Scapeghost was Level 9's final adventure game, and it is in the same format as the existing ones, which makes for a text parser with additional graphics. Puzzles require instructions to be given to other characters. The game is split into 3 days, each of which can be played independently of each other - November Graveyard, Haunted House and Poltergeist.

418763.overview: Shoot Em Up is a 1st Person Shooter where you control a target on the screen and shoot waves of aliens over various levels. You can scroll the screen left or right as you search for the aliens to shoot and once you have shot enough you move to the next level. The aliens will throw cubes at you and if one hits then you lose part of your shield gauge and when it reaches zero you lose one of three lives. Other gauges to keep an eye out for is your fuel gauge which slowly decreases and ammo which decreases when you fire. There are icons scattered around for all three gauges and when shot increase them.

418764.overview: Sleepwalker is an exciting, fast-paced game for the Atari 400/800 with 24K and one joystick, In Sleepwalker you must maneuver your sleepwalker. Fred, to avoid the refrigerators which come at you in an incessant stream, hit the stegosaurus sandwiches and drink the bottles of cactus juice to stay alive in this bizarre game. So get set and good luck!!

418765.overview:
The player controls a space shuttle which can move vertically up and down. Satellites, asteroids, UFOs, and Rockets stream from the right of the screen. The shuttle is armed with a laser that fires to the right, and can shoot down oncoming dangers. The shuttle has the ability to catch satellites with the mechanical arms that protrude from the top of the vehicle. After several rounds of incoming objects, the player enters a meteor storm with a number of fast moving asteroids to avoid, and then returns to regular speed.

The player has a total of 3 shuttles, when all are lost, it's game over.

418766.overview:
The major battle in Western Theater of American Civil War fought on April 6-7, 1862 near church Shiloh in Tennessee was the bloodiest battle between Union and Confederate forces. Historically Union forces lead by Maj. Gen. Ulysses S. Grant won in the battle and finished Confederate's hopes to block the Union invasion of northern Mississippi.

The game is played as Confederates, as Unions, both sides, or having the computer choose. Two scenarios are available: the Campaign Scenario April 6-7 (Confederate's attack and Union's counterattack after Union supporting forces arrival) and First Day Scenario April 6 (Confederate's attack only). There are three difficulty levels and five levels of different options such as Conf/Union Ammo Supply, Union Arrival, Conf/Union Effeciency.

During war gameplay you move the troops on the map with rectangular grid using your tactical/strategical skills by turns, after that combat is flowing, and statistical results of the combat are shown. Map represents nature of the locality. Each turn takes some amount of time. Your actions increase your score according to successfulness.

418767.overview:
The major battle in Western Theater of American Civil War fought on April 6-7, 1862 near church Shiloh in Tennessee was the bloodiest battle between Union and Confederate forces. Historically Union forces lead by Maj. Gen. Ulysses S. Grant won in the battle and finished Confederate's hopes to block the Union invasion of northern Mississippi.

The game is played as Confederates, as Unions, both sides, or having the computer choose. Two scenarios are available: the Campaign Scenario April 6-7 (Confederate's attack and Union's counterattack after Union supporting forces arrival) and First Day Scenario April 6 (Confederate's attack only). There are three difficulty levels and five levels of different options such as Conf/Union Ammo Supply, Union Arrival, Conf/Union Effeciency.

During war gameplay you move the troops on the map with rectangular grid using your tactical/strategical skills by turns, after that combat is flowing, and statistical results of the combat are shown. Map represents nature of the locality. Each turn takes some amount of time. Your actions increase your score according to successfulness.

418770.overview:
Shape Up! is a 1-player educational game for small children.

The player controls Shapeman, who needs to sort shapes as they fall from above. The player needs to move squares to the trucks, triangles to the cats, circles to the people, and rectangles to the buildings. Players can also make their own images using these 4 shapes.

418771.overview:
The 2nd and final in the series of detective/problem solving games for kids. Armed with your Snoop-mobile, the snoopNET computer, a wrist-radio, flashlight and pen and paper, you're the detective who must solve the case of Lilly, the missing dolphin.

The game requires logical thinking, planning, and note taking as you slowly comb the neighborhood gathering clues and evidence. Once the suspect is properly identified, use the snoopNET computer to accuse and ensure that justice has been served.

418772.overview: A Skramble style horizontal shooter released in Italy in Go Games n.8 (Aprile 1986) as "Bomber". Shoot or bomb fuel to keep your reserves up and see how far you can penetrate the dangerous and twisting shaft. What do you do when you want to write a game that is better than Airstrike, Protector and Caverns of Mars? Easy, you write one that combines the best of all three and add some improvements. That is basically what Shaft Raider is. You start with five ships in a horizontally scrolling landscape as in Airstrike but the first thing you notice is that the graphics of the cavern or the shaft are much better. In the early stages there are no missiles being launched but you have to bomb or shoot fuel and ammo dumps and stationary missiles whilst avoiding flak. The flak is quite dangerous, appearing at random, sometimes right on top of your ship giving you no chance to maneuver. As you enter and progress down the shaft there are space mines bobbing up and down which you cannot shoot, just avoid. When there are three or four in quick succession it is quite a feat of navigation to weave between them. Shortly after the space mines come force fields to navigate through followed by the Protector- type buildings with fuel tanks embedded in their roofs and the first of the launching missiles. Some of them you can shoot but others you must avoid, there is no way of telling which. So it goes on. More and more hazards, narrower passages and more difficult force fields until you reach the Master Mine.

418773.overview:
You're in a beautiful, colorful galaxy. Your mission is to conquer all the planets for the Galactic Federation and then go to the next galaxy. The player controls a ship that can move in all directions. The player must watch out for Clone Robot Ships that will relentlessly pursue the player, destroying every planet in their path. If an enemy ship reaches the player, it's game over. The player can scroll off one edge of the screen to appear on the other side to avoid the pursuing enemy.

The player can release nukes, which act as mines to destroy the enemy clone ships if hit. The player can select the number of nukes they have at the beginning of each level. There is also an option for shields, which will protect the player from their own nukes.

418774.overview: Three of the key battles of the American War of Independence are recreated here. The British army and American patriots can be played by either human or computer (with 3 skill levels). Each side's level of reinforcements and ammunition can be set on a 5-point scale. The smallest and shortest battle is Bunker Hill, while the Battle of Monmouth is distinguished by harsh weather, and Saratoga requires a different fighting style to the highly regimented one the British unsuccessfully used.

418775.overview: Huge scrolling star map plus a computer-referenced sky atlas.

418778.overview:
The Earth is under attack! Flying saucers from Procryn 5 as assimilating its molecular structure for use back on their planet. They must be stopped! Strapped into your rocket suit, you cruise high into the stratosphere, waiting to blast the Alien ships to smithereens; but watch out for the Ram Star if you want to get back alive!

The player controls a spaceman who can fly in all directions and fire horizontally. Alien saucers fly about stripping pieces of the ground away. The player tries to shoot all saucers. The saucers are harmless for the player, but the Ram Star will intermittently fly across the screen, and will take the player's life if hit.

Contain the bonus game Mutant Bats, an arcade game where the player bounces a ball off a horizontally moving bat at the bottom of the screen. The goal is to destroy all blocks located above. Every missed ball costs a life.

418779.overview: Maze game that uses gravity physics and slingshot effects.

418780.overview:
The first in a series of 'edutainment' titles long before the portmanteau term was popularized by marketing executives, Snooper Troops had younger players trying to solve the mystery of "The Granite Point Ghost", an entity that is trying to scare the Kim family out of their new home.

Using the SnoopNet computer, players will comb the streets of the neighborhood looking for clues, and investigating people's houses while they're away. Speed is of the essence, as if your Snooper Troop is caught when the owner of the house returns home, you could be thrown off the case for good!

The title encourages players to keep facts on people, map the neighborhood, review clues, receive special messages, and ultimately, find enough information to accuse and convict the criminal trying to chase the Kim family out their home.

418781.overview:
This interactive fiction game is a trilogy of the Level 9's adventures Snowball, Return to Eden, and Worm in Paradise. These had previously been released for some but not all of these systems.

Silicon Dreams can be played as three separate games, but to obtain the maximum number of points, you must complete them in order (carrying your score from one adventure to the next). Snowball has graphics for the first time, and the other two games have more graphics than before, and some longer text descriptions are added to all 3 games.

Snowball: As Kim Kimberley, your mission is to safeguard the colonization ship Snowball 9 and its passengers. When you are awakened prematurely from hibernation, you know something's wrong!

Return to Eden: Your objective is to get into the new city of Enoch, and stop the Eden robots from destroying Snowball 9.

Worm in Paradise: You have to find as much information about the city as possible, obtain money, and then become a member of the governing party of Eden.

418783.overview: Educational program teaching what is going on inside your computer.

418785.overview: Repackage of two previous Antic Software releases.

418786.overview: The player has been employed as traffic coordinator at a busy space port, and must usher all ships of the Inter-galactic Fleet through the port for refuelling and refitting. If the player makes a mistake the fleet is destroyed. There are 9 levels of difficulty from space private to admiral. At the lowest level, the player sees 2 ships fly into the space port, and must use the menu at the bottom to make sure they exit in order they entered. At higher levels, more spaceships enter, the time to have them exit is limited, the space port can rotate, and ships can exit from both ends of the port.

418787.overview:
As captain of the U.S.S. Starship, you're our last hope for destroying the invading Oralop spaceships intent on capturing this galactic outpost of democracy!

Gameplay is on an 8 x 8 grid of 64 quadrants, and the player has limited fuel and stardates to complete their mission. Each quadrant can contain a sun which must be navigated around, a friendly star base which the player can recharge, and enemy Oralop vessels. The player's vessel is armed with long range sensors to investigate adjacent quadrants, or can call up a galactic report to review all quadrant the player has occupied.

The player does battle with Oralaps, and is armed with photon torpedoes and phasers. The player has access to a status report on the condition of their ship's equipment. The player must control their shield status

418789.overview: Spider Eater is a musical learning game for children. The spiders are invading the treble clef, and the child needs to hit the right notes to protect it from the spiders. Children will develop ear, eye, and hand coordination, and develop relative pitch and interval perception. Children will also learn the notes on the keyboard, the musical staff, and note and pitch recognition. The game supports the Koala Pad which is a touch tablet that interacts with the game.

418797.overview:
This  is a repackaged version of "Renaissance" previously released by UMI,

The aim of this game is to change all your opponents counters to your colour or have more counters on the board at the end of the game. To change the colour of your oppositions counters, you place a counter opposite another of your counters vertically, horizontally or diagonally with no set distance. Any opposition counters in between gets changed to your colour. You and the other player takes it in turns until the game has ended and the player with the most counters win. This version of the game has various options before and during play. You can choose a skill level of the computer (1-9), change colour, make the computer play a counter, take back a move, set the board into various situations and change the skill level. You use the joystick to move a cursor to place a counter.

418799.overview:
Includes slightly reworked versions of the following programs, all re-released without authorization:

* Computer Football Strategy
* Strikes'n Spares
* Sunday Golf

418800.overview:
By the 37th century, human expansion had reached far across the galaxy. Security of the frontiers of these worlds was the responsibility of Colonial Star Command. During the latter years of the 37th century, first contact was made with probes of the non-human Empire. To prevent Empire penetration of inner worlds, a number of Colonial Starbases were established to create buffer zones, designed to hold enemy fleets for several days, until large Colonial reinforcements could arrive. This tactic worked well for some time, until 716 CD, when a large fleet of Empire vessels were spotted in Sector Hyperion. The armada has already captured 18 frontier worlds, and Starbase Hyperion is the remaining defensive position preventing invasion of inner worlds. As captain of the Starbase, you must hold out superior numbers until Colonial reinforcements arrive, to drive back the invading forces.

The player must defend Starbase Hyperion for a total of 15 turns until reinforcements arrive. A separate winning conditions is destroying all enemy vessels. The player starbase is located in the center of a 360 degree field. During each turn, the player controls their base's energy output to power ships, probes, strengthen defenses, or strengthen shields. The player can also produce power banks, which create future energy reserves. Excess energy can also be stockpiled for future turns.

Ships can be deployed, and if they come within range of enemy vessels, automatic combat will occur. The amount of energy devoted to ship creation determines the quality of vessel produced. Ships can be returned to the starbase for full repairs. Probes are capable of detecting displaying the location and strength of distant enemy vessels, and must also be moved into position. Probes can also be detonated to create an energy field which may slow or destroying incoming enemy vessels.

There are total of 6 difficulty levels, and the player chooses the difficulty level and number of enemy ships at the beginning of each scenario. Difficulty level effects the strength of alien vessels from small fighter squadron to dreadnaughts. The player receives a final score based upon their efficiency at the end of each battle.

418802.overview:
Utilizing a birds-eye view of the golf course, the player chooses their club and the direction of their shot. The choice of club has no effect on a swing other than distance, and all shots go straight in the direction prescribed, with no wind or other factors affection play. Hazards including sand traps and water are present.

When the player lands a ball on the green, gameplay shifts to a 2-dimensional side-view, where the player must select a shot strength between 1 and 50. Greens have hills, which can influence how much strength is required, and the player will overshoot the hold if too much strength is directed. Score is maintained throughout all 18 holes.

418806.overview: The Star Voyages are two part electronic mini-novels, in which you play the role of Captain Karl Turk of the Starship Venture. The Star Voyages are more than the usual "take object" adventure. They are original short stories written by the author. In part 1, you are introduced to your crew and have the opportunity to familiarize yourself with the Venture. Unexpectedly, a mysterious asteroid is discovered. You must prepare to investigate. In part 2, you discover a race of alien humanoids, who are outcasts of their own civilization. You soon learn of an evil race of huge aliens referred to as "the others". You then must prepare yourself for the inevitable clash of your two cultures!

418947.overview:
Treasure Island Adventure is the third in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

You have come across a map giving the exact coordinates to Treasure Island, and have determined it is in Long John's writing. You have spent your savings on passage to the island, where you hope to find his treasure.

During the player's adventure, they must explore the island, and more importantly the extensive underground cave network. The player must locate a number of treasures, including: a gold ring, a priceless Ming vase, a treasure chest, and more. These must be returned to the building on the island with the goal to obtain a total of 258 points. Points are also awarded for each new area discovered. Naturally, the player has a lamp with limited fuel to hinder their adventure.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save or restore feature.

418948.overview:
Alien Adventure is the second in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

Based upon the movie Alien, you are the sole survivor of the Nostromo, on a mission to deliver a cargo of oil to the Earth. A crash landing has left you stranded on an alien planet, and you must gather supplies to enable you to return to the Earth aboard your escape shuttle. During the player's adventure, they must avoid the aforementioned alien, while looking for artifacts and supplies hidden through the alien planet and a crashed alien vessel that is remarkably similar to that seen in the original movie. These include oxygen, a map to the Earth, an alien teleporter, fuel, a diamond, an alien gem, and more. The difficulty level determines how many turns available until the alien arrives and kills the player.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save or restore feature.

418949.overview:
Arabian Adventure is the first in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

Princes Jasmine has been kidnapped by the evil wizard Rex. He has taken her to his castle, where she is imprisoned. You must find the wizard's castle, and destroy him, to rescue the princess.

During the player's adventure, the must seek help from a genie, explore hidden caves, and travel across the sea. Enemies including skeletons, cyclops, and sea monsters block the player's path. Ultimately, the player finds the princess in miniaturized form, and must be brought back to her home, where a potion must be created to return her to normal size.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save or restore feature. Various monsters are found at specific locations, which can be defeated in text-based combat. Combat consists of attacking the enemy, but there are no hit points.

418950.overview:
Jack the Ripper Adventure is the fourth in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

As a constable of Scotland Yard, you have been assigned to patrol the Whitechapel section of London to seek out Jack the Ripper and put an end to his murderous crimes of passion.

Game has a basic day/night cycle, with each night lasting 50 turns and each day lasting 90 turns. Certain events will only occur during the day or night. During their adventure, the player must explore the streets of London gathering evidence regarding the identity and location of Jack the Ripper.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save or restore feature.

418951.overview:
Crime Adventure is the fifth in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

While minding your own business outside the local arcade, you see Mrs. Fenwick get kidnapped by hoodlums. The player must explore the local neighborhood gathering clues to her location. During the adventure, the player must explore the Fenwick's home, as well as that of a gypsy, and visit several local stores looking for clues and supplies. Ultimately, Mrs. Fenwick is located underground beneath Mr. Fenwick's putting green. Using cunning, the player must return her to her forlorn husband.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save or restore feature.

418952.overview:
Around the World in Eighty Days Adventure is the sixth in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

The player tries to complete the feat of recently successful Phileas Fogg, by also traveling around the world in eighty days using available technologies of the time. The player starts in London, and takes a hot air balloon ride to Barcelona, Spain. From there, they explore the desert, and take a yacht to Marseilles, France. In Marseilles, the player must outsmart punks, and take the train to Italy. In Italy, the player must scare a fat woman with a mouse to take a steamship to Bombay, India. While attempting to take a train across India, the player becomes stuck in the jungle, and must befriend some elephants to travel across the subcontinent. While traversing the jungle, the player rescues an Indian princess, and arrives in Ahmadabad, India, and then takes a train to Calcutta. The player just barely makes a steamship to San Francisco, and travels across North America, getting some help from Tinkerbell along the way. The player ultimately arrives in London with one day to spare.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save or restore feature.

418968.overview:
Klondike Adventure is the ninth in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

You have come to the Klondike in search of Yukon Bill's riches, but you must beware the bitter cold, and other dangers of the Arctic. Game is a treasure hunt, where the player must locate a gold nugget, gold flakes, a pickax, a fur coat, and the last will and testament of Yukon Bill. All these five items must be returned to the starting area for a perfect score of 100 points. During the adventure, the player will beat up a walrus, steal a dead man's boots, meet Santa Claus, steal Rudolph's nose, rob a vending machine, pan for cold, and crawl around inside an oil well.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is a save and restore feature.

418969.overview:
Windsloe Manor Adventure is the eighth in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

The world famous 'Pumpkin Man' has been kidnapped, and is being held captive in the dungeon of Windsloe Mansion. The owners of the mansion are Mr. Winsloe and his wife, a known witch. Your mission is to get inside the mansion, find the Pumpkin Man, and return him to your starting location. The player must locate the secret passage within the Blairs' next door mansion, and delve deep within Winsloe mansion. Within, the player may gain extra points by slaying three ghosts, a vicious dog, the moss man, a vampire, an alien, a giant wasp, and the witch Mrs. Winsloe. Finally, by returning with the Pumpkin Man, the player is victorious, and receives a score based upon the number of baddies they killed. Maximum score is 210.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save or restore feature.

418970.overview:
James Brand Adventure is the tenth in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

You are secret agent James Brand, and the President's has been kidnapped by Dr. Death. Can you save him before it's too late? There's danger lurking at every turn. The player starts in their secret base, but must evade a number of potential threats to their life during the adventure. From dealing with the brakes being cut on their car, a motorcycle lancer, and bombings, there is constant danger. The player must visit the Kit Kat Club, and outsmart the Madame with a poison drink, and then sail to Dr. Death's secret island. There, the player must survive Dr. Death's human pinball machine and a deadly game of pool, eventually defeating him with a cyanide tablet. Finally, the player finds the President hidden beneath a golf course, and must defuse a bomb before it's too late. Gameplay consists of multiple small vignettes. During the adventure, almost any wrong move will result in the player's death.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is a save and restore feature.

418971.overview:
Witches' Brew Adventure is the eleventh in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

You have just arrived in an enchanted forest, and your goal is to rescue the princess. The player must explore a witches' cottage, which contains numerous magical items and secrets, as well as the surrounding forest and mountains. The goal is to gather the necessary ingredients to create three magical potions, the brews of invisibility, shrinking, and growth. Using the player's wits and these magical ingredients, they player must plant a beanstalk to allow them access to the giant's castle high in the sky. There, they must outsmart the giant and rescue to princess imprisoned within the castle. Dangers include the witch of the cottage, her cat, a malevolent axeman, wild animals, and the giant who live up in the sky.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is a save and restore feature.

418972.overview:
Arrow One is the thirteenth in series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

It's been 3 years now, 3 years since your mission into deep space. Your name is Adam Trent, explorer, trouble-shooter, and all around good guy for the Federation of Space. Your journey aboard Arrow One has come to an end: an uncharted planet the council asked you to explore. Slowly you descend onto this strange new world.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save and restore feature.

418973.overview:
Robin Hood is the fourteenth in series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

You play as Robin Hood of Sherwood forest, with the goal of performing great deeds with your band of merry men. At the start of the adventure, Robin starts alone in Sherwood Forest, and must recruit Will Scarlet, Little John, Friar Tuck, and Allan A. Dale. As Robin explores the forest, he will intermittently find rich merchants, who can be relieved of their bags of gold. These can be used to buy arrows, a new bow, or a new sword, and the player is also awarded for giving gold to the poor. After recruiting all four merry men, the player must find horses for his crew, and they will all ride to Nottingham. There, the player can enter the archery contest in disguise, and if they are successful, will be awarded with a golden arrow. As he is awarded, Robin's disguise falls off, and he is arrested by the Sheriff, only to be saved by his band of men. Upon returning to Nottingham, Robin finds Maid Marion has been kidnapped, and must kill the men guarding her. After that, the player is chased by the Sheriff of Nottingham, who can be dispatched with an arrow. Finally, the player must meet King Richard and be knighted to achieve victory.

The player is awarded points for 5 deeds: Giving money to the poor, winning the archery contest, saving Maid Marion, killing the Sheriff, and meeting King Richard.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save and restore feature.

418974.overview:
Titanic is the twelfth in series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

You are the captain of the luxurious ship the Titanic. During its maiden voyage, you crash into a giant iceberg. Your goal is to rescue as many people as possible onto the lifeboats of the vessel, as well as save any valuables you can find. The game consists of many locked rooms on the main deck of the vessel, most of which contain a frightened passenger. The player must find the keys to all the locked doors, and convince the frightened passengers to join them on a lifeboat. Passengers include a frightened girl, Mrs. Vanderbilt, a Chinese speaker, a librarian, a lady with her toe stuck in the tub, a waiter, a drunken woman, an angry woman, a baby, a sleeping steward, a deaf woman, and a number of frantic passengers. If the player tries to put too many passenger on a boat, it will sing, and the player loses points for all people on the boat. Finally, the player must locate several expensive luxury items to achieve maximum score, and get themselves on the last awaiting lifeboat. The player receives points for each passenger saved and item found, for a total score of 3175

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is a save and restore feature.

418975.overview:
The Mouse that Ate Chicago is the fifteenth in series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

The greedy and warped mind of Professor Rainier Frankenfeld has led to the creation if an enlarging ray, which can make any object several hundred times its normal size. As the professor prepares to enlarge a diamond, several mice scamper into the field. Four mice, Sam, Maja, Puji, and Fiji have been enlarged to gigantic size, and begin to wreck havoc about Chicago. The player, while out joyriding in their truck in the outskirts of Chicago, runs out of fuel. It is around that time, that they start to notice the surrounding mouse-related devastation. The player must use trickery to defeat the four mice to protect the inhabitants of Chicago.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save and restore feature.

418976.overview:
Menagerie Adventure is the sixteenth in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

While out on a pasture, you see strange vehicle ahead that appears to be a spaceship. As you are drawn closer, the door opens and you walk inside. Stepping inside, the door suddenly closes, and the alien vessel rapidly accelerates into space. You realize you've been captured aboard an alien zoo ship, and you are to be their newest attraction. Captured aboard the alien vessel, the player must explore the ship, and use the assistance of other alien creatures from throughout the solar system to escape your prison. Each of these creatures from different planets have unique skills which will allow the player to finally access the navigation control of the alien vessel, and reroute the vessel back to Earth, allowing their escape.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save and restore feature.

418977.overview:
The Deadly Game is the seventeenth in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

A note arrives at your doorstep one summer evening. Your uncle Sir Henry Vanderbilt from the province of Burmesia has passed. You have been invited to the reading of his will in one weeks time. Upon arriving at your Uncle Henry's mansion in Burmesia, you meet a number of your snobby relatives whom you had hoped to never meet again. Uncle Henry's will states that each of you is to receive one million dollars, on the stipulation that you spend the night in his mansion. He further notes, that if anyone does not spend the night, or is deceased by the morning, the remaining money will be split among the surviving inheritors. Being a group of money loving degenerates, the inheritors begin to go about killing each other off.

The player starts in their room, and must avoid tarantulas and poisonous gas. As the player explores the mansion, numerous deathtraps must be avoided, most of which are unpredictable before the player's death.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save and restore feature.

418978.overview:
The Dalton Gang is the eighteenth in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

Newly arriving in a generic Western town, you have been elected sheriff my the mayor simply on the merits of showing up. At the start, the bank comes under attack by the Dalton gang, and in the ensuing firefight you kill two members. The remaining gang takes off with the mayor, and you must head out into the desert to rescue him. The player must purchase supplies and navigate the dangerous desert, finding water along the way, and avoiding vicious rattlesnakes. There, you stake out the Daltons' cabin, ambushing them as they leave. The Daltons flee, and Bob is captured deep in an abandoned mine, along with the mayor and the stolen money from the bank. The player must then return to town, locking up Bob Dalton and returning the stolen cash. Then, the player must disguise themselves and arrest Emmett Dalton, and lock him up as well.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save and restore feature.

418979.overview:
Alaskan Adventure is the nineteenth a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

You're in Alaska, standing in the snow. Around you, fifteen treasures are hidden. Some are buried in the snow, others are cached in nearby igloos. Some are in even stranger places, and you will need considerable ingenuity to get them. The player must travel to 8 separate frozen areas via dogsled. The player's goal is to return all the items to the trading post, and many of the items are found in local snow drifts or stolen from the nearby Inuit community. Along the way, the player's dogsled team will often break down, requiring the player to feed them, get them water, or treat their illness to continue to the next area.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save and restore feature.

418981.overview:
Danger is by Business is the twentieth and final in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

You are Sarasota Sam, Secret Agent. The American Ambassador to India's daughter has been kidnapped into the wild jungles of the subcontinent. You must brave the dangers of the jungle, while harassing and avoiding the numerous natives within the jungle. Eventually you come across the kidnappers in their tent with the kidnapped woman. The player must disarm the kidnappers, and bring the woman to the safety of the American embassy.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save and restore feature.

419208.overview: On the distant planet of Thule water must be conserved and you must control the constructor robots to build the resevoirs. The only problem is that the native predator of Thule, a kind of giant starfish, is deadly and will stop you if it can. Can you store enough water to ensure that Thule survives? A Qix style game by Murvyn Pikestriker, however there have been unsubstantiated claims that it was an unauthorized rip off of a Tom Hudson game called Fill'er up!.

419314.overview:
Showdown Hockey! is a 1-2 player Ice Hockey game for the Atair 8-Bit computers. It was developed and published by Canadian company Aussemware in 1991.

The game just features one player vs the other player's goalie.

419837.overview: You must guide M.A.D. (Miniature Android Debugger) through the circuits of a silicon chip at the heart of a futuristic arcade machine, picking up all the stray bits, and shooting the bugs. Beware of the deadly Glitch.

419867.overview:
Sky Writer is an educational action game for children.

You steer the plane "Sky Writer" and while you are flying, clouds with words in them are drifting by.

Your goal is to combine two root words to create a compound word that fits the description at the top of the screen. For example the description says "Well-mannered guy" then the answer would be "gentle" + "man" = "gentleman" For each correct root word you score 10 times the number of the level you're at.

If you choose a wrong root word or if you get the correct root words in the wrong order your plane will crash. Your plane will also crash if it flies into a raincloud, which will appear from level 3 onwards. If you run out of fuel your plane will also crash. There is no way to refill your fuel, so you better hurry.

The game has 8 levels and you can choose whether you want to start from level 1 or level 3 in the options menu. When you complete a level, you score 10 the number of the level you're at, multiplied by the number of fuel units you have left. Should you make it all the way through level 8, you score an additional 5 percent of your total score for each unused plane and you'll also receive a bonus message.

420004.overview: The Stock Market is more than a game. One to six players can play for millions of dollars. Trade for stocks, follow graphs of your stocks for each trading day. Go to the bank and borrow money but remember - it's got to be paid back with interest. Become a billionaire or a pauper. It's up to your skill and cunning. High quality graphics.

420006.overview:
Stockmarket is a 1 - 6 player metal trading game for multiple systems.

Each player starts with $1000, and each player can buy or sell lead, zinc, tin, and gold. High prices are likely to go down and low prices are more likely to go up. The price of each share is set at approximately half of its maximum value at the beginning of the game.

Newsflashes randomly appear, which can cause drastic changes in metal prices, and the players can gain bank interest or encounter capital gains tax. There are 4 levels of play difficulty.

The game ends when one or more players have $1 million.

420013.overview:
This compilation contains 4 different strategy games: 

Robot Patrol - The player controls a robot who must travel to the 9 planets and their moon to capture 10 criminals in a limited time frame. The player can move towards or away from the sun, and must scan each location for a criminal. The player can employ 3 different weapons with varying energy requirements and accuracy to capture the criminal.

Star Merchant - An interstellar trading game, where the player must move to different ports with their vessel, buying and selling items for profit. Fuel, docking, and crew costs are subtracted every time the player visits a port. Contraband can lead to high profit, but a risk of losing everything.

Civil War - A text-based US Civil War simulator, the player controls the Confederacy, and most allot money to their food, ammunition, and salaries, which directly effects their war readiness. The player can choose from 4 types of attacks and defensive maneuvers to counteract the Union. Success depends on choosing the correct maneuver based upon enemy moves.

Convoy - You serve as a naval lieutenant, with the goal of escorting 15 convoy vessels and a destroyer from Britain to a port in Russia to supply relief against the Nazis. Along the way, the player can encounter Nazi submarine and air attacks. During these attacks, the player has several minigames, where they attempt to shoot down planes or hunt submarines. If they are unsuccessful, ships and supplies are lost.

420161.overview: Starball is a side scrolling arcade game. The aim of the player is to escape of trapped prison by properly using the acquired items. The player controls the direction and the speed of the ball. Flip the ball from the obstacle causing considerable acceleration. With each passing second energy of the ball is constantly decreasing. To top up the energy the player has to get a diamond. The player must avoid closing barriers, fire or swamp fields. To get into evacuation area the player has to get through many closed doors. The correct order of using the found keys is the only way to access the final position. Except of the keys and diamond the player may find few other useful items, such as a time bomb, temporary resistance to fire, canisters and hammers.

455824.overview:
You are Captain of the Starship Herman, and your mission is to pilot your spaceship to Mars, and recover the archaeologist Dr. Grady and other crew members, whom were lost in the Martian underground during the previous Explorer II mission. Mars was once inhabited by two races, the reptilian Meshim and the insectoid Zanti, and Dr. Grady holds the key to understanding what happened to these two races.

Your mission begins with outfitting your spaceship for the long voyage. You must ensure you have enough fuel, food, and oxygen for the long trip, as well as other supplies you'll need on the Red Planet. You must also choose your crew members, as each has special skills which are essential for survival on the harsh Martian climate.

455833.overview:
Survival is a 1- 6 player strategy game for the 8-bit Atari.

You are stranded on the alien world of Coryphire. Your only chance of survival is to travel 340 km to an abandoned research station. Unfortunately, the planet has difficult terrain and is populated by several carnivorous and hungry life forms. Your skill and cunning are your main tool. You will salvage as much as you can from your starship and begin your trek. With a fair amount of luck, your supplies should last. If you hurry!

The player has a total of 6 days of food to reach their destination, and each day is divided into 3 turns: morning, evening, and night. Each player starts at a preset location on the overhead map, and they can only move during daylight. The player chooses their starting weapons with a limited weight restriction, with each piece having distinct ammo load.

Movement occurs on an overhead map, where the player specifies which direction to travel each turn. There are 8 terrain types, which effect movement speed and possible monster encounters. The player has 6 movement turns per round. During movement, the player can encounter dangerous alien lifeforms. These are fought in ranged and then close combat, where the player must select which weapon to use, and how much ammo they have remaining. Each hit will sap a single health point from the player or enemy.

468605.overview:
Stargate was the 1982 sequel to Williams' smash arcade hit Defender.  Stargate's name was changed to Defender II sometime after 1984 due to some kind of copyright problem.  As with most sequels, Stargate didn't change the game formula that helped make the original game a hit.  Instead Stargate expanded on the formula...

Stargate added a number of new features to the Defender formula including new enemies, new abilities, and of course stargates!  Stargates allow players to instantly warp from one area of the level to another, which can be very handy if used right.  Stargates can also be used to warp forward levels if certain amounts of humanoids are carried into them.  The ability to score bonus points for carrying multiple humanoids is also a new feature first introduced in this game.

Other new abilities include the Inviso power, which is basically a super cloaking device.  Using Inviso makes your ship invisible and allows it to pass through all enemies and their shots.  However you can still shoot while "Inviso", so make the most your Inviso time.  Stargate also includes the ability to enter Hyperspace.  Entering Hyperspace is just as dangerous as it was in defender, and while it can save your life in an emergency it can also blow you to smithereens.  Use the Hyperspace option sparingly!  

Stargate is unique among Atari 8-bit games as it uses the original arcade title screen, including all the arcade colors, fonts, and options.  Of course all of this wasn't by coincidence, programmer Steve Baker had an original Stargate arcade machine in his house so he could perfect the 8-bit version.  According to Steve when he was done you could stand back 10 feet from the screens and not be able to tell the difference.

The options on the title screen allow the player to affect a whole range of game variables:
 
Number of Players	Pretty self explanatory.  This can be set to 1 or 2 players
Number of Ships	Another no brainer.  This is the number of lives each player has.  The value can be set from 1 to 9.
Inviso Time Per Ship	This option sets the amount of time your Inviso power lasts.  The value can be set from 4 to 20.
Extra Ship Every	This option allows the player to set the frequency at which extra lives are awarded.  This value can be set from 1,000 to 50,000.
Men Needed To Warp	This option affects the number of humanoids the player needs to carry into a stargate to warp to the next level.  This value can be set from 2 to 9.
Last Wave Warp Allowed	This option allows the player to set the last wave number in which the wave warp (mentioned above) can be used.  This value can be set from 10 to 99 (hey you don't want to skip all the levels do ya?).
Master Control Difficulty	This option controls the overall difficulty of the game.  The value can be set from 1 to 5.
 
 
While Stargate may have beautiful graphics and an arcade accurate title screen, this version has major problems with slowdown.
